name: External iliac artery
notes: Continues as the femoral artery distal to the inguinal ligament.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Femoral artery
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Superficial epigastric artery
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Superficial circumflex iliac artery
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Profunda femoris (deep femoral) artery
notes: Main supply to the thigh muscles; gives medial/lateral circumflex femoral aa. and 3-4 perforating branches.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Medial circumflex femoral artery
notes: Major supply to the femoral head/neck (retinacular vessels) -- clinically important in femoral neck fracture avascular necrosis risk.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Lateral circumflex femoral artery
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Perforating arteries (1st-3rd, of profunda femoris)
notes: Pierce adductor magnus to reach the posterior thigh; supply the hamstrings segmentally.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Descending genicular artery
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Popliteal artery
notes: Continuation of the femoral artery through the adductor hiatus into the popliteal fossa; deepest structure there.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Superior lateral genicular artery
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Superior medial genicular artery
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Middle genicular artery
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Inferior lateral genicular artery
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Inferior medial genicular artery
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Sural arteries
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Genicular anastomosis (around the knee)
notes: Collateral network providing alternate flow to the leg if the popliteal artery is occluded at the knee.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Anterior tibial artery
notes: Passes anteriorly through a gap in the interosseous membrane at the top of the leg, into the anterior compartment.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Anterior tibial recurrent artery
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Dorsalis pedis artery
notes: Continuation of anterior tibial a. onto the dorsum of the foot; palpable (dorsalis pedis pulse).
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Arcuate artery
supplies_or_drains: dorsal metatarsal arteries -> dorsal digital arteries
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Deep plantar artery (of dorsalis pedis)
notes: Dives into the sole to complete the plantar arch.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Posterior tibial artery
notes: Larger terminal branch of the popliteal artery; descends in the deep posterior compartment with the tibial nerve.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Fibular (peroneal) artery
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Medial plantar artery
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Lateral plantar artery
notes: Larger terminal branch; forms the plantar arch.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Plantar arch
supplies_or_drains: plantar metatarsal arteries -> plantar digital arteries
notes: Deep arch analogous to the hand's deep palmar arch; predominantly the lateral plantar a., completed by the dorsalis pedis' deep plantar branch.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
